name: Temporal Fastest and Earliest-Arrival Paths
problem_statement: Find time-respecting journeys minimizing elapsed duration or arrival time in a directed temporal graph.

normalization: Preserve all declared vertices, including isolated vertices.
Preserve direction; an undirected projection must be explicitly requested.
Declare the treatment of self-loops and parallel edges before execution; an adapter must reject unsupported cases.

problem_inputs.name: objective
problem_inputs.description: Arrival time or last-arrival minus first-departure duration.

problem_inputs.name: duration_attribute
problem_inputs.description: Nonnegative traversal duration stored in each edge attributes object.

required_outputs.name: values
required_outputs.description: Best temporal objective per reachable vertex; null when unreachable.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether all requested objectives were computed.

solution_semantics.objective: Optimize the declared temporal journey objective, allowing waiting between edge events.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact objective values; chronological path enumeration alone is insufficient.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Output identities refer to the normalized input; any multiplicities must follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No output order or choice among equally valid optima is required unless specified by an input.

validation_rules: Every next departure is no earlier than the previous arrival.
Compare against a time-expanded-graph oracle on small inputs.
edge_cases: Multiple events between the same endpoints remain distinct.
Zero-duration edges require an explicit equal-time convention.

correctness: Every next departure is no earlier than the previous arrival.
Compare against a time-expanded-graph oracle on small inputs.
